Native cell inspection now includes alwaysVisible Blob tileDesc outside FOV. The actual window text uses explicit Messages composition for base/custom terrain and each displayed Blob description; unknown/hidden blobs stay excluded by the native predicate.

The selected water preview uses the native water texture frame at the inspected known cell. This UI image remains tied to the same cell subject; terrain knowledge and public descriptions are separate facts, with no raw frame serialized.
MobTitle attaches the selected object/mob name and sprite even when OBJECT omits health/buff children. Keep the public title/portrait without inventing omitted object statistics.

MobTitle creates health/buff widgets but v4 attaches them only when OBJECT is absent. Capture must read attached children only: Vault objects expose no sample or buffs from unattached fields, while ordinary mobs retain laid-out bars and buff symbols.
MobTitle applies fixed title color to the selected native name; name/image identity is separately attached and is not inferred from tint.

WndUpgrade conditionally tints previews for unidentified/known-uncursed/known-cursed states and labels for upgrade/curse infusion. Preserve these native knowledge cues and unknown markers rather than RGB or hidden levels; they are distinct from fixed separators.

WndUpgrade confirm/back preserve native readiness, forced consumption, upgradeItem return value and selector reopening. Re-reviewed v4 durability previews using levelFrom/levelTo and infinity only above 100; reading preview/options must not execute an upgrade.

WndUpgrade title/icon, remaining quantity, current/result item images and level text retain native ? and +1? unknown markers. Upstream durability previews now use levelFrom/levelTo and >100 infinity. Capture reads this window instead of recalculating hidden item stats.
WndUpgrade anonymous declarations fingerprint native confirm/back callbacks. Actual button/text sites are separately semantic; scanning cannot invoke upgrade or selector reopen.

WndUpgrade lays out fixed preview backgrounds, item/label positions and vertical separators. These geometry sites add no predicted stats or known/unknown state; conditional tint, text and item sources are separate.

Reviewed all new projection branches: native water-backed decoration, publicly visible/remembered native objects without creature facts, and alwaysVisible environments restricted to native known cells. No save/private audit reads or dynamic callbacks were introduced.

Reviewed native OBJECTs are represented as object with projectile_collision=character only when their actual sprite is eligible and FOV or native visibleOutOfFFOV+known-cell rules allow it. Neutral Mimic disguise branch remains separate and gains neither collision semantics nor creature health/buffs.

CUSTOM_DECO_WTR maps to native WATER base terrain; secret terrain conversions and existing knowledge checks stay intact. Custom visual description supplies its separate public semantic shape without leaking atlas state.

Current map.env mirrors native WndInfoCell: normal blobs need FOV, while native alwaysVisible blobs may survive visited/mapped fog. Unknown cells stay absent; only native public tileDesc/type is emitted, never volume or timers.

Reviewed current UI changes remove the obsolete three-width health fallback and bind publicly projected native OBJECT subjects separately from characters. Existing source/draw ownership, frozen text, full subject uniqueness and operation gates remain intact.

A same-frame projected object may bind its actual unique Mob only when OBJECT and projectile_collision=character are explicit and it is not a neutral Mimic. Object subjects do not populate creature buff references; absent/ambiguous bindings remain unresolved.

The old HealthBar fallback is removed because current native HealthBar implements GameplayStatus with four displayed widths including required incoming_dot. Existing semanticStatus reads current source-selected HUD samples; it never invokes Char.incomingDOT or fabricates zero DOT.

" + "_-_ 103 days after Shattered v1.1.0

" + "v1.2.0 focused on a number of improvements to try and make Shattered play just as well for desktop users as it does for phone users. While these changes weren't perfect right at launch, they played a major role in making Shattered feel like more than a mobile port and helped it have a successful launch on Steam.
" + "
" + "One big change for desktop users that's external to the game itself was native executables. Previously Shattered's desktop version required a separate installation of Java to run. After v1.2.0, I started making versions of Shattered with built-in Java instead. This meant that most users could just download the game and run it, much nicer.
" + "
" + "v1.2.0 also included a variety of little additions and tweaks. Most of them are self-explanatory, but the badge additions in particular were timed with the game's release on Steam so they could tie into steamworks achievements and give newer players a little more to do.")

" + "v0.9.2 added the first tier of talents that were applicable through the later stages of the game.
